rationale: This is a mechanical splice of two archive signals — "DebtIssue EarningsShortfall AccrualStress" (fmb -3.67, alpha -0.039) with its accrual leg simply lagged one period, exactly the lag already tried in "AccrualFirst ExternalIssuer" — so it is a cosmetic timing variant rather than a substantively different mechanism, and lagging the accrual leg makes the information staler without addressing why the contemporaneous version's alpha stalled.

The financing leg is identical to the archive's "WorkingCapital DebtBeyondEarnings" and "DebtIssue EarningsShortfall AccrualStress," while the accrual leg is just a broader balance-sheet restatement of the recch+invch buildup already used there (and of the Δact−Δche core in "DebtAdjusted CurrentAccrual Issuer"), so it is a within-family leg swap whose incremental content over the standard accrual/asset-growth anomaly is unclear.

The economic direction is unidentified — the archive's "OperatingLiability EquityIssuer Stress" tells the opposite story (rising payables as supplier stretching predicts underperformance) with the same external-funding leg, so a payables *decline* being bearish is a post-hoc sign flip rather than a disciplined hypothesis, and the construct is otherwise a decomposed piece of the already-tested "ReceivableTradeCredit FundingGap."

The financing leg (RANK(csho growth) − RANK(sstk/at)) is byte-for-byte the archive's "NonDepAccrual NoncashDiluter," and the accrual leg is byte-for-byte the archive's repeatedly used −(txach+aoloch)/at, making this a pure two-signal crossover with no new mechanism.

This is the archive's "EquityFunded Receivables Inventory Build" (fmb -2.09, alpha ≈0.00) with the inventory term dropped and the accrual leg lagged, i.e., a narrower and staler version of an already-weak signal whose lag-based cousins ("LaggedEquity WorkingCapitalDeterioration," "PostFunding AccrualDeterioration") also failed to produce alpha.

The TREND-based measure of *increasing* capital-market dependence is a genuinely different time-series characterization from the level, sum, and ACCEL versions already tested, and the sign is internally coherent, though it remains a derivative refinement of a heavily mined accrual×external-financing family and the accrual leg is the plain Sloan measure.
